subject.title: Security: agents.defaults.tools/sandbox are inert — an agent resolved without an agents.list entry runs with the full tool profile and no sandbox

question: Should any supported turn ingress be allowed to execute under an agent ID that is absent from `agents.list`, including IDs derived from explicit session keys?
rationale: Current routing and sandbox behavior refute the broad report, but source still permits an unconfigured ID to survive session-scope parsing; whether that is an intentional ephemeral identity or a security-boundary violation is a product and trust-model choice.

options.title: Reject unknown identities
options.body: Fail the turn before tool construction whenever the resolved agent ID is absent from a non-empty configured agent list, with focused tests for CLI, bindings, gateway turns, and explicit session keys.

options.title: Support ephemeral identities
options.body: Define unconfigured identities as supported and prove that they consistently receive the global sandbox and global tool-policy baseline across every ingress.

options.title: Confirm no reachable ingress
options.body: Retain current behavior only after runtime or exhaustive source proof shows that unsupported callers cannot submit an unconfigured identity to the agent execution path.

recommendation.title: Reject unknown identities
recommendation.body: Fail the turn before tool construction whenever the resolved agent ID is absent from a non-empty configured agent list, with focused tests for CLI, bindings, gateway turns, and explicit session keys.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the relevant sandbox, agent-scope, routing, and exec-policy security surfaces.
